newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania leu ends weaker vs dlr, money market up.
newsitem.headline: Romania leu ends weaker vs dlr, money market up.

text.p: Romania's leu ended Friday down to 6,450/500 to the dollar on a hard currency-squeezed market which failed to react to major economic indicators for 1996 released at mid-day by the National Statistics Board.
The leu opened at 6350/400 to the dollar in the morning.

Traders said the market was still digesting Thursday's jump in the one-week refinancing rate to 90 percent from 81 percent, which triggered an upswing of short-term money market rates to some 85-90 percent from 80 percent earlier in the week.
They said leu-dollar interbank prices remained weaker than retail rates of around 6,350 at currency shops, which were plagued by leu shortages.
Operators said there was scope for a further leu slide in the coming weeks after the 8.7 percent drop this week and a 58.5 percent plunge from January 1.
"The leu was overvalued last year and despite the recent downswing exporters still hold on to their earnings eyeing better prices," said a trader with a dealer bank.

Traders said they expected a further tightening of the central bank's monetary policy early next week when the bank might lift its key discount and Lombard rates -- now at an annual 50 and 90 percent respectively.

"Central bank wants to create a hunger for leu currency to fight inflation and make the leu more attractive," said one trader, adding that he expected the Lombard rate to move up to 130 percent and the discount to some 70-75 percent.
Year-on-year inflation rose to 56.9 percent last December, nearly triple the 20 percent 1996 target agreed with the International Monetary Fund.
